name: Centralization trap

subjectOf.text: Separating internal on-chain governance from external legal relations maximizes decentralization while preserving real-world enforceability, thereby avoiding the fatal centralization that undermined earlier DAO concepts.
subjectOf.abstract: This duality maximizes decentralization while preserving enforceability in the real world, avoiding the fatal centralization that has undermined earlier DAO concepts.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The UDLC DAO Operationalizing a Continuously Evolving Universal Digital Law Codex Through Weighted (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5887242

subjectOf.text: By rejecting any requirement for a legal entity, board, or registered agent, the UDLC DAO escapes the centralization trap that undermined earlier DAO legal structures while remaining enforceable through standard private international law.
subjectOf.abstract: By rejecting any requirement for a legal entity, board, or registered agent, the UDLC DAO preserves pure code-based governance while remaining enforceable through standard private international law mechanisms.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The UDLC DAO Operationalizing a Continuously Evolving Universal Digital Law Codex Through Weighted (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5887242
